Novyy Buh Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Mykolaivska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Novyy Buh's Jewish community likely emerged by the mid-19th century, when a synagogue already operated; the population reached 1,962 (15 percent) by 1897 and 3,600 (19 percent) by 1910, supported by six synagogues, a Talmud Torah, and a private vocational school. By 1913, Jews owned both of the town's pharmacy goods warehouses, two photo studios, the only cinema, and more than 40 merchant stalls. The community survived a 1919 pogrom organized by N.A. Grigoriev, and received material assistance from J.-I. Shneerson, likely connected to the Chabad Schneerson family documented at several other sites in this collection; the population fell to 934 by 1923 and 269 by 1939. Following the August 1941 occupation, the Germans murdered the town's 28 remaining Jews on May 14, 1942, though a religious community remained active as late as 2005. This cemetery, which existed by 1910, was barely damaged by Nazi forces during WWII, per local historian A. Kyslyy, before being demolished by Soviet authorities in the 1970s; one resident recalled finding two Jewish gravestones while digging a pit on the site in the 1980s.
